- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model shows strong upward bias, cap forecast rise at 3–5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots; apply a 1–2 day lag correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply a 2–3 day mean reversion buffer: forecast = 0.8×previous 7-day avg + 0.2×current sentiment-weighted trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.67/0.33 alternation, model tends to overfit short-term sentiment; dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% unless sentiment is strongly trending.
